chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darradj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what the Imam recites in the two rak'ahs at the end of the prayer. He said: 'With the Opening of the Book (Al-Fatiha), and those behind him do not recite, and the man recites in them if he prays alone with the Opening of the Book.'

key_terms.فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: The Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting Al-Fatiha in the last two rak'ahs of prayer for the Imam, congregation, and individual?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the jurisprudential debate regarding the necessity of reciting Al-Fatiha in the final two rak'ahs, specifically distinguishing between the Imam's obligation and the congregants' silence (samt) in the Shia tradition. It further confirms that individual prayer requires full recitation, reinforcing the principle that the Imam's recitation suffices for the followers in congregational settings. This ruling is foundational for understanding the structure of Fajr and 'Asr prayers in Shia fiqh.
